Given that $r$, $s$ and $t$ in the above diagram are parallel, find $m∠1.$
question.worked_solution:
Consider $∠2$ and $∠3$ in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14244234/assets/44552b4c1624cd049769bf672d510c33f5cfdb53a8726ada5e0ed4cafea11b64.png)

Note that $∠2$ and the angle whose measure is ${80}^{∘}$ are corresponding angles formed by the same transversal. Therefore, 

$$
m∠2={80}^{∘}.
$$

Similarly, note that $∠3$ and the angle whose measure is ${50}^{∘}$ are corresponding angles formed by the same transversal. Therefore, 

$$
m∠3={50}^{∘}.
$$

Let's add these measures to our diagram:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14244234/assets/4672d1aa0d64c5af11c85bb90f834a440eb53a4b9e490ce1b0cb22b5306f4f27.png)

The angles $∠1$, $∠2,$ and $∠3$ combined give a straight angle. So, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠1+m∠2+m∠3 & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠1+{80}^{∘}+{50}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠1+{130}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠1 & ={50}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$
